title: Skipping terms: a shorter chain of algebraically closed sets with the same normality condition
author: J. de la Nuez, González, Zaniar Ghadernezhad, Paolo Marimon, Michael Pinsker
work: Minimal and intrinsic topologies on monoids of elementary embeddings
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Lemma 5.7 (source label 'skipping terms'): given a chain of algebraically closed sets of even length that satisfies one of two intersection conditions (a common intersection at every other triple, or containment in a single invariant algebraically closed set at every other pair), there is a chain of half the length whose normality condition is contained in that of the given chain for some group element, and the two cases can be preserved. The unit is above ordinary PhD qualifying level because the counted proof is a sixty-line combinatorial construction rather than a citation: it splits into the two cases, builds the shorter chain by taking intersections of the even members and moving the odd ones with a group element, verifies the normality containment by a direct computation over the intersection monoid, and then re-establishes the preservation of the intersection pattern in each case. Manipulating chains of algebraically closed sets inside a homogeneous structure and controlling the normality semigroup along the shortened chain is research-level model theory of monoids of elementary embeddings, beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
